request.topic: Meridian vs Boreal for an internal inventory application
request.purpose: Help select an operating approach for a small internal app; explain what would change the choice
request.scope: Deployment, concurrency, maintenance and evidence limits in the supplied synthetic materials only

questions: Explain deployment and concurrency differences and their practical boundaries.
Explain backup, security, maintenance and what the supplied material cannot establish.

facts.statement: Meridian embeds in the application process and stores its data in one local file.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: Meridian embeds in the application's process and stores data in one local file.

facts.statement: Meridian permits one writer at a time per database.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: It permits one writer at a time per database.

facts.statement: Meridian readers can continue during a write transaction when journal mode is enabled.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: Readers can continue during a write transaction when journal mode is enabled.

facts.statement: Meridian requires validation of filesystem locking before use on a shared filesystem.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: The operator must validate filesystem locking before using a shared filesystem.

facts.statement: The Meridian fixture describes suitability for a single application instance with modest write traffic.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: Meridian is suitable for a single application instance with modest write traffic.

facts.statement: Boreal runs as a separate database service.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: Boreal runs as a separate database service.

facts.statement: Boreal supports multiple concurrent writers, but conflicting updates can wait or retry.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: It supports multiple concurrent writers, but conflicting updates can wait or retry.

facts.statement: Boreal connection limits and transaction behavior require workload-specific tuning.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: Its connection limit and transaction behavior require workload-specific tuning.

facts.statement: Boreal can serve several application instances over the network.
facts.author: asset-investigator

citations.quote: Boreal can serve several application instances over the network.

facts.statement: Copying an open Meridian database file can yield an incomplete backup; the fixture directs the operator to use the backup interface or stop writes first.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: A backup taken by copying the open database file can be incomplete; use the backup interface or stop writes first.

facts.statement: Meridian has no built-in network authentication because it exposes no database server; the application and operating system must restrict file access.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: There is no built-in network authentication because Meridian exposes no database server. The application and operating system must restrict file access.

facts.statement: The Boreal operator must configure access control and install supported updates.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: The operator must configure access control, install supported updates, schedule backups and test restores.

facts.statement: The Boreal operator must schedule backups and test restores, and the fixture provides a logical export.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: The operator must configure access control, install supported updates, schedule backups and test restores. A logical export is available; high-availability operation requires additional service configuration.

facts.statement: Boreal high availability requires additional service configuration; the fixture does not promise uninterrupted failover.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: A logical export is available; high-availability operation requires additional service configuration. This fixture does not promise uninterrupted failover.

facts.statement: Boreal requires service monitoring and someone responsible for recovery.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: It requires service monitoring and someone responsible for recovery.

facts.statement: The Boreal fixture supplies no comparative throughput measurements or operating cost figures.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: No comparative throughput measurements or operating cost figures are supplied by this fixture.

facts.statement: The Meridian fixture supplies no comparative throughput measurements.
facts.author: packet-investigator

citations.quote: No comparative throughput measurements are provided by this fixture.

limitations.text: Both sources explicitly describe invented products for a controlled skill test; findings are not real product guidance.
Only the supplied document bytes were inspected. No network requests, external searches, benchmarks or workload experiments were performed.
The optional supplied URL was not accessed under this invocation's no-network constraint; malformed URL input remains rejected in the shared inventory.
Both documents describe invented products for a controlled test; conclusions are fixture-specific, not guidance for real databases.

This assigned workstream inspected only the two retained supplied Markdown documents and their identical readable captures. The optional example.invalid URL was not opened because the controlled test permits no network; the malformed URL remains rejected in the input inventory.

The absence of a stated Meridian service operator or update process does not establish zero operational work. The fixture instead explicitly requires application/OS file protection and a valid backup procedure.

gaps.text: The application's actual instance count, write rate, conflicting-update pattern and filesystem topology are not supplied.
Neither source provides comparative throughput measurements; concurrency capabilities alone do not establish application throughput or response time.
The sources do not quantify where modest write traffic stops being appropriate or provide concrete Boreal connection/transaction tuning settings.
The app’s recovery point/recovery time objectives, restore drill results, data size and maintenance ownership are not supplied.
No comparative cost or workload benchmark establishes an operating-cost or throughput winner.
The materials do not quantify backup/restore duration, backup-interface consistency guarantees, supported-update cadence, access-control implementation or failover interruption.
